title: Detection of a Millimeter Flare from Proxima Centauri
question: Does the 1.3 mm emission from Proxima Cen require dust belts, or is it explained by stellar flaring and coronal emission?

what.value: Photospheric flux at 1.3 mm of 74±4 uJy from SED emission model

evidence.quote: the expected photospheric flux at 1.3 mm is $74\pm4$ $\mu$Jy
Deep ALMA surveys at millimeter wavelengths have placed strong constraints on the expected number of faint background sources in an image (cite: Carniani:2015)

recipe.method: Natural-weight clean image and uvmodelfit point source fit to visibilities, combined and per SB/scan

recipe.goal: Variability, spectral index and polarization of quiescent emission
recipe.method: Excess variance of per-scan fluxes; XX and YY imaged separately for |Q/I|; flux in 225+227 and 239+241 GHz windows for alpha
Image the 13 ACA observations individually, then fit visibilities in 2 s intervals in the flare scan; alpha and |Q/I| in 5 s bins
Optically thin gyrosynchrotron relation alpha = 1.22 - 0.9 delta

evidence.quote: yields a total flux density of $101\pm9$ $\mu$Jy
At peak brightness, the flux density reaches $100\pm4$ mJy
a luminosity of $2.04\pm0.15\times10^{14}$ erg s$^{-1}$ Hz$^{-1}$ at 1.3 pc

evidence.loc: 4.1 Nature of the Detected Stellar Flare

not_stated_but_needed: clean cell size, image size, niter, and threshold
how the spectral index and uncertainties were derived
how flux density in the 2 s and 5 s bins was extracted
how the number of background sources was computed from the counts
missing_for_reproduction: uvmodelfit initial guesses and time-binning details
score_reason: Data public and approach simple, but CASA version and fit details are missing.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, simple recipe and numeric results (flare peak, spectral index).
